metadata.summary: MedMNIST is a collection of standardized, pre-processed medical image classification datasets covering 18 (v1) / 20+ (v2) tasks across diverse modalities (dermoscopy, X-ray, OCT, pathology, chest CT, retinal, etc.), at small uniform resolutions (28x28 / 64x64 / 128x128 for 2D, 28x28x28 for 3D). It aggregates ~708K 2D images and ~10K 3D images from existing public sources, intended as an educational benchmark for reproducible ML rather than a clinical-scale resource.
metadata.purpose: Intended as an educational benchmark for reproducible ML rather than a clinical-scale resource.
metadata.avoided_uses: Real-world clinical deployment; high-stakes diagnostic decision-making due to low resolution and inherited label quality.

papers.title: MedMNIST v2: A Large-Scale Lightweight Benchmark for 2D/3D Medical Image Classification

modality.scope: Multi-organ, multi-disease classification tasks across diverse anatomical and pathological domains.

ethics.privacy_measures: All data are de-identified prior to inclusion; no protected health information retained.
ethics.legal_compliance: Complies with licensing terms of upstream sources; no direct IRB documentation provided by MedMNIST team.

extraction.notes: 基线卡仅来自 dataset_catalog.xlsx 真实元数据；其余字段需论文/README 或人工补充。

known_limitations: Tiny image resolution (e.g., 28x28) — not suitable for clinical interpretation or deployment.
Designed for education/reproducibility, not real-world deployment.
Class balance and label quality inherited from upstream sources.
No standardized demographic reporting across sub-datasets.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Pre-processing includes uniform resizing, normalization, and format conversion; no synthetic data generation.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Not representative of clinical imaging practice due to resolution constraints and aggregation from heterogeneous, non-probabilistic public sources.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Present in several sub-datasets (e.g., PathMNIST, OrganAMNIST), inherited from upstream sources.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Limited generalizability beyond controlled benchmark settings due to low resolution, lack of clinical context, and unknown population representativeness.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: Subgroup coverage (e.g., age, sex, ethnicity, geography) is not standardized or reported across sub-datasets.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic and clinical metadata largely missing or inconsistent across sub-datasets.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Detection, segmentation, report generation, or any task requiring spatial fidelity or clinical-grade inputs.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Aggregates existing public medical imaging datasets to enable standardized, lightweight benchmarking for educational and reproducibility purposes.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregates ~708K 2D images and ~10K 3D images from multiple existing public sources.

population.target_population: Patients and cases represented in underlying public medical imaging datasets (e.g., dermatology, radiology, ophthalmology, pathology cohorts).

attribute_recording.unknown_proportion: Demographic attributes (age, sex, ethnicity) are not reported or standardized across constituent sub-datasets.

annotation.annotation_method: Labels derived from original source datasets; no new annotation performed by MedMNIST team.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels inherited from upstream public datasets; quality and consistency vary by source.
annotation.label_noise_description: Label quality and class balance inherited from upstream sources; DermaMNIST labels known to contain noise per original publication.
